beats.title: Lesson 15 — Reading the Alert Buffer
beats.say: Welcome back to CybICS. When an incident is over, someone has to reconstruct what happened. In this lesson we put on the forensic analyst's hat and read the intrusion detection system's alert buffer as evidence.

beats.head: The alert buffer is the record
beats.body:
Each IDS alert is a timestamped fact: who, what, which target, and which technique. Read together, they reconstruct the attack.
  • The analyst answers: one attacker or many?
  • What was the sequence — recon, then impact?
  • Which ATT&CK techniques were used?
beats.say: Each alert the intrusion detection system records is a timestamped fact: who, what, which target, and which technique. Read together, they let the analyst reconstruct the attack. The questions are always the same. Was it one attacker or many? What was the sequence of events? And which ATT and CK techniques were used?

beats.caption: Generate the incident: recon...
beats.say: First we generate an incident to analyse. The attacker scans the OpenP L C, the reconnaissance phase.

beats.caption: ...then impact
beats.say: Then the attacker moves to impact, flooding the high pressure tank register. Now there is a full incident in the buffer to reconstruct.

beats.caption: Read the evidence: the full IDS alert buffer
beats.say: Now the forensic read. Every alert points to a single source, one seven two dot eighteen dot zero dot one hundred. The order tells the story: reconnaissance first, a port scan and a S Y N flood, then impact, a Modbus flood and unauthorized writes. One attacker, a clear sequence, four techniques.

beats.head: The reconstruction
beats.body:
• Attacker: a single source, 172.18.0.100.
  • Timeline: recon (T0846, T0836) → impact (T0836, T0855).
  • Target: the OpenPLC at 172.18.0.3.
That reconstruction — source, timeline, techniques, target — is exactly what an incident report needs.
beats.say: The reconstruction writes itself. A single attacker at address one hundred. A timeline that runs from reconnaissance to impact. The target was the OpenP L C. And the techniques map straight onto MITRE ATT and CK. Source, timeline, techniques, target: that is exactly what an incident report needs, and it is the analyst's job to read it out of the evidence.

beats.caption: Submit the flag in the CybICS dashboard - on the attack machine
beats.say: We complete the forensics challenge on the dashboard, submitting the analyst flag we earned by reconstructing the attack from the alert buffer.

beats.head: What we learned
beats.body:
• Preserve the alert log — it is your evidence.
  • Reconstruct the timeline and attribute it to a source.
  • Map each step to ATT&CK so the report is actionable and comparable.
beats.say: To recap: preserve the alert log, because it is your evidence. Reconstruct the timeline and attribute it to a source. And map each step onto ATT and CK, so the incident report is actionable and can be compared with known adversary behaviour.
